claim_ceiling.rationale: with about 21 test clips the clip is the experimental unit and frames are correlated sub-samples; a frame or clip bootstrap is refused and the claim verb is bounded to 'consistent with', never 'demonstrates' or 'significant'

claim_scope: deterministic programmatic mechanics only; no capability or natural-data claim
direction: candidate > rate_matched_random (candidate places the same firing budget better)
metric: onset F1 at DCASE plus or minus 200 ms collar, greedy one-to-one, strict point-wise PR

multiplicity.rationale: four variants scored against one fixed test split inflate the family-wise error, so each variant is held to the Bonferroni-adjusted alpha 0.0125. With five paired seeds the smallest achievable one-sided sign-flip p is 0.03125, which exceeds that adjusted alpha, so no single variant can clear family-wise significance from this family alone. This is a preregistered statistical wall: a variant may still register a SESOI-exceeding effect for triangulation, but family-wise promotion needs more seeds and bias-independent reproductions, never a larger claim squeezed from n equals 5

operating_point_rule: the swept firing budget whose firing fraction is closest to the train-set onset density; a fixed rule set before scoring, using only train labels, never a val or test F1 argmax
promotion_bar: promote only when the registered SESOI is exceeded AND the one-sided sign-flip p clears the Bonferroni-adjusted alpha AND at least three bias-independent reproductions triangulate the same direction; a single run, and any run at n equals 5 across this four-variant family, can never promote

sesoi.rationale: Cost-benefit SESOI on onset F1. The candidate and the rate-matched-random control fire the same count K at equal FLOPs, so the amortized training cost C_train (8274960000 FLOPs, equal to 206874 downstream-firing equivalents at C_down = 40000 FLOPs) buys nothing but the F1 advantage of learned placement over free random placement. At the operating firing fraction 0.080 the per-frame downstream saving against always-on is 36800 FLOPs, so the gate does not even repay C_train until N* = 224,863 frames (about 6.2 hours of audio). Given that deployment scale, the smallest F1 win worth registering is one that is both measurable above the pseudoreplication floor and economically meaningful. One recovered onset moves pooled F1 by about 0.0019 (1 / 538 test onsets), and one test clip (the experimental unit) is about 25.6 onsets, i.e. an F1 scale of 0.0476. The chosen SESOI of 0.05 sits an order of magnitude above the per-onset granularity (so it is not measurement noise) and at about one test clip's worth of correctly-placed onsets (so a win below it recovers less than one clip of onsets more than free random firing and does not justify carrying a trained module over the zero-training control). A win below the SESOI is not promotable even if the one-sided sign-flip p clears alpha.
sesoi.selection_method: cost-benefit (docs/ESCS_DEEP_RESEARCH.md Q5a option 3), same as base prereg

sign_flip_test_plan.statistic: mean of paired per-seed F1 deltas (variant minus rate_matched_random)
sign_flip_test_plan.test: exact sign-flip permutation, one-sided, upper tail

variants.hypothesis: A post-decision refractory window (collar-width non-maximum suppression on p_fire) forbids a second fire inside an already-covered collar, so the fixed budget spreads to distinct onsets instead of clustering adjacent fires on one high-energy region, raising distinct-onset recall over rate-matched-random at matched budget.

Retraining the value-of-computation target on local flux novelty (a frame's flux minus its causal neighborhood median) rather than absolute energy teaches the gate to fire on change points, not loud steady regions, so its placement beats free random placement.

Partialling out raw magnitude by dividing the features by a causal running-energy EMA before the gate removes the loud-region confound, so a sustained high-energy passage stops repeatedly attracting fires and the budget lands on separated onsets.

A recurrence-aware online feature that penalizes firing shortly after a prior fire (the frames-since-last-fire gap in the online state) makes the gate withhold adjacent fires and distribute the budget across separated onsets, beating uniform random placement.
